Foundation

Meaning behind the logo

Brand direction

How First Seed should feel.

Growth-oriented

Communicate progress, compounding, and the idea that wealth develops over time.

Youthful and modern

Clean layouts, friendly illustrations, simple language and interactive experiences, without looking like a children's game.

Trustworthy and secure

Money is personal. The brand should feel safe, transparent and credible to young users and to their parents.

Supportive, not intimidating

Avoid the private-banking image of exclusivity. Make financial guidance accessible and judgement-free.

The core concept

Wealth-building,
as a habit that starts early.

The opportunity is to make wealth management more accessible to professionals at every stage of their financial journey, instead of treating investing as something reserved for people who are already wealthy.

Young professional

time on their side

Growing family

building for the future

Senior professional

wealth for the next generation

Long-term wealth →
Core differentiator

The platform does not simply help people manage money.

It helps them learn how to build wealth.

Managing money

Balances, budgets and spending.

Building wealth

Learning, saving for goals and investing, with guidance.

Growth & LearningThe heart of the product.
Target market

Two customer groups.

20s to 30s40s and above
2030405060+

Young professionals

  • In their career-building phase.
  • They have disposable income, but limited knowledge when it comes to investing.
  • Many are entrepreneurial, eager to invest, and willing to experiment, even take risks.
  • Many will eventually start families. Building for the future becomes even more important.
  • Time is their greatest asset, and we can help them capitalize.

Senior professionals

  • They have achieved a certain level of success, and have accumulated assets.
  • Many have prioritized moving up in their careers, putting children through school, acquiring real property, and getting health and life insurance, with some investments on the side.
  • Many have a mish-mash of investments, from shares and equity in companies to mutual funds, bonds, government securities, dollars and gold.
  • They want continued income streams even after retirement.
  • Their window is getting shorter, and at the same time, wealth building becomes even more imperative.
  • Generational wealth is the dream, and they want their children to be financially savvy earlier in life.
The concept

Mobile-first,
from first investment
to long-term wealth.

One platform that allows users to:

See their complete financial picture

A dashboard that shows the real-time value of all income, investments, savings and debt.

Access real-time information on available investment opportunities

The app is linked to leading banks and e-wallets, brokerage houses, fund managers, insurance and pension services, and the Philippine Stock Exchange for market information.

Get real-time information and AI-powered insights

Stay updated on markets and investment opportunities, and be empowered to build wealth-building strategies with the help of AI analysis.

Make and execute investment decisions from their phone

No need for a separate wealth planner, relationship manager, stockbroker, fund manager, financial advisor or insurance agent, and no need to fill out so many forms with each transaction.

Business Opportunity Matrix

From Competitors

No one connects every institution for the mass market.

Banks, brokers and insurers each show only their own products. Only private-bank clients get one view of their wealth.

Good advice is gated by wealth.

Relationship managers and full planning start above a wealth threshold, while small investors get generic products.

Open finance and AI make it possible.

The BSP Open Finance Framework, consented data-sharing, real-time payments, and generative AI as a personal CFO.

Business model. One hub for every institution, free to start.

Our company
Competitors
Trends
Adjacencies
Value chain
Networks
One hub connecting banks, brokers, fund managers, insurers, real-estate and government platforms, plus peer referrals. Families are a secondary network.
Private banks grow through relationship managers and HNW referrals; only those clients get a consolidated view. Each bank, broker and insurer app shows only its own products. GCash and Maya rely on huge wallet bases.
Open finance and data-sharing; wealth aggregation; super-app consolidation; the great wealth transfer to Millennials and Gen Z; community investing.
Aggregators that put many suppliers in one place: Booking and Skyscanner, insurance and loan comparison sites, Plaid-type data networks.
SuppliersAsset managers and custodiansCustomersProfessionals who refer peersDistributorsEmployers, communities, bank and e-wallet partners
Partners
Banks (BDO, BPI, Metrobank, RCBC, Security Bank, Bank of Commerce), brokerages (First Metro Sec, COL Financial, BPI Trade, Philstocks), fund managers, insurers, PSE data, the Bureau of the Treasury, PERA providers, real-estate and alternative platforms, e-wallets, credit and tax data.
Each institution partners only for its own products: banks with fund managers, brokers with PSE, robo-advisors with ETF providers, private banks with global asset managers. No one connects across all institutions for the mass market.
Open finance and Banking-as-a-Service; white-label wealth-as-a-service; fintech and licensed-incumbent partnerships as the standard model.
HR and payroll platforms, insurtech, tax and accounting services, real-estate platforms already in the customer's financial life.
SuppliersFund houses, KYC vendors, cloud and market dataCustomersProvide consented financial dataDistributorsEmployers (payroll) and banks
Pricing models
Freemium with three revenue streams: a free dashboard and basic AI analysis, a low fee when users transact or invest, and an optional subscription for in-depth analysis. No large balance needed for advice.
Private banks: high minimum balances, advisory or AUM fees, plus sales loads on funds. Robo-advisors: low AUM-based fees. GInvest and Maya: very low minimums.
Fee compression; demand for transparent fees; hybrid subscription-plus-transaction models; younger investors unwilling to lock up large balances.
SaaS freemium and tiered subscriptions (Duolingo, tax software); telehealth pay-per-consult; fitness apps replacing costly trainers.
SuppliersFee-sharing and referral fees to keep user fees low (to validate)CustomersFree to start, pay as they transact, upgrade for depthDistributorsEmployer per-seat licensing (B2B2C) as an add-on
